deep.reconstruction: The page has no mathematics. It is the title page and first paragraph of 'Mechanik des Ohrs. Aus dem Nachlass von B. Riemann', the posthumous essay edited by J. Henle and printed in 1867 in Henle and Pfeufer's Zeitschrift für rationelle Medicin; it is also in Riemann's Gesammelte Werke. The previous page's printer's imprint ('Gedruckt bei E. Polz in Leipzig'), the editorial asterisk footnote, and the even calligraphic hand suggest this is a copy prepared for or from the edition, not a Riemann autograph. Section 1, 'Über die in der Physiologie der feineren Sinnesorgane anzuwendende Methode', lays out the method of the essay. (1) Beyond the general laws of nature, the physiology of a sense organ needs two special foundations. One is psychophysical: the empirical determination of what the organ does (its 'Leistungen'). The other is anatomical: the investigation of its structure. (2) Hence there are two routes to knowing its functions. One can start from the structure and deduce the laws of interaction of its parts and the effect of external stimuli. Or one can start from the observed performances and try to explain them. (3) The first route infers effects from given causes; the second seeks causes for given effects. (4) Following Newton and Herbart, the two routes are named analytic and synthetic. The following page begins 'Synthetischer Weg. Der erste Weg liegt dem Anatomen am nächsten', so the first route is the synthetic one. It then argues that this anatomical route is unreliable for microscopic sense organs, because their physical properties cannot be measured precisely. That forces arbitrary appeals to analogy or teleology. This sets up Riemann's preference for the analytic route: start from the ear's precise performances and infer the necessary mechanical conditions. He goes on to apply this to the ossicular chain and the tympanic membrane, against Helmholtz.
errors: The last sentence as transcribed calls the first route (causes to effects) 'analytic' and the second (effects to causes) 'synthetic'. This contradicts Newton's usage (Opticks, Query 31: analysis goes from effects to causes, composition/synthesis from causes to effects). It also contradicts the next page, which heads the first route 'Synthetischer Weg'. As far as I recall, the printed text reads 'den ersten Weg den synthetischen, den zweiten den analytischen nennen'. Either the copyist inverted the terms or the transcription misreads the image. As I read the image the order is analytischen/synthetischen, so this is probably a slip in this copy. It should be checked against the autograph and the printed version.

results.what: Methodological distinction for sense-organ physiology: a synthetic route (from anatomical structure to function) versus an analytic route (from measured performance back to the mechanism required). Riemann favours the analytic route for the ear.
results.modern_name: Forward modelling versus inverse problem / reverse engineering; Newtonian analysis–synthesis applied to physiology
results.usually_credited_to: The analysis/synthesis distinction goes back to Pappus and Newton, with Herbart's usage cited here. Its application to the ear is Riemann's, in 'Mechanik des Ohres' (published posthumously by Henle, 1867).

deep.surprise_reason: This is the opening of Riemann's published posthumous essay 'Mechanik des Ohres', which is well known and included in his collected works. The page is purely methodological prose with no mathematics, and it appears to be a copy for the edition rather than new material.
transcription_corrections: The left-margin deletion '[-Ist.-]' is uncertain; it may be a struck section mark or 'Lit.'/'Ist.'. It is illegible as a word.
'(eine psychophysische)': the parentheses are in the manuscript. The sense is 'eine psychophysische, die erfahrungsgemäße Feststellung der Leistungen des Organs'.

'den ersten Weg den analytischen, den zweiten den synthetischen' should be verified against the image and the printed text. The context (next page 'Synthetischer Weg. Der erste Weg …') and Newton's usage require 'synthetischen … analytischen'.
The hand appears to be a fair copy by an editor or copyist, not Riemann's autograph; note the title 'Aus dem Nachlass von B. Riemann' with an editorial footnote asterisk.
The stamp reads 'EX BIBLIOTHECA REGIA ACADEM. GEORGIAE AUG.' (Göttingen University Library).
